chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from the one who mentioned it, from Al-Khashab, from Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir, from Dawud al-Raqqi, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he asked for water. So when he drank it, I saw him bewail and his eyes filled with his tears. Then he said to me: 'O Dawood! May Allah curse the killers of Al-Husayn (peace be upon him). And there is no servant who drinks water, so he remembers Al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and the People of his household, and curses his killers, except that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, writes for him one hundred thousand good deeds, and deletes from him one hundred thousand sins, and raises for him one hundred thousand levels, and it is as if he has liberated one hundred thousand persons, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will resurrect him on the Day of Judgment as cool-hearted.'

key_terms.أَهْلَ بَيْتِهِ: The People of his household (Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ: Imam Al-Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet
key_terms.ثَلِجَ الْفُؤَادِ: Cool-hearted (a state of tranquility and relief)
key_terms.قَاتِلَهُ: His killers (referring to those who killed Al-Husayn)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for remembering Imam Al-Husayn while drinking water?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the profound spiritual connection between the physical act of drinking water and the remembrance of Imam Al-Husayn (peace be upon him), illustrating the Imam's deep emotional attachment to the Ahl al-Bayt. It establishes a specific merit (thawab) for this practice, promising immense rewards such as the forgiveness of a hundred thousand sins and the elevation of a hundred thousand degrees, reflecting the Shia tradition of linking daily sustenance with eternal spiritual benefits.
